title: Rational-point transport and its scheme-Frobenius normalization
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Fix $m\geq1$ and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with induced geometric point $\bar y:s\to X$. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ ($n\geq1$), $\mathcal O_E$ or $E$, use the finite, derived-complete integral, or rationalized constructible category and its pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $G_\Lambda=Lg_{X,\Lambda}^*$ and $J_{y,\Lambda}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}L\bar y_\Lambda^*$, with point fiber functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

Throughout, specify the integral pullback-composition and pullback scalar comparison families by the strict-system realization formulas of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]; these are the choices of the comparison isomorphisms in [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. 

One has $g_X^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$. Define $t_{y,m,K}:J_{y,\Lambda}K\to J_{y,\Lambda}G_\Lambda^mK$ by the $m$ successive point transports of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on $L\bar y^*K$, followed by the canonical pullback-composition identification for that equality (at integral level use [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and rationalize at $E$). This is natural: for every morphism $u:K\to L$,
$$J_{y,\Lambda}(G_\Lambda^mu)t_{y,m,K}=t_{y,m,L}J_{y,\Lambda}(u).$$

At finite level let $\Phi$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], let $\kappa^{(m)}:L(\Phi^m)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g_X^m)^*$ be the specified multiplicative comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], and let $\rho_{y,m,K}:J_{y,\Lambda}K\to J_{y,\Lambda}L(\Phi^m)^*K$ be the canonical pullback-composition identification from $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$. Under the identification $L(g_X^m)^*\cong G_\Lambda^m$, one has
$$t_{y,m,K}=J_{y,\Lambda}(\kappa^{(m)}_K)\rho_{y,m,K}.$$
Here $\kappa^{(m)}$ uses the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization, with no scalar rescaling. This equality commutes with quotient-coefficient transitions as an equality of the specified maps on simultaneous strict reduction systems. Its integral realization and rationalization give the same equality at the integral and rational stages. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on reductions of an integral object is required.

For finite coefficient fields $E\subset M$, write $T=-\otimes_E M$, let $d_K:T G_E^mK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_M^mTK$ be the iterated canonical pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], and let $b_K:J_{y,E}K\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{y,M}TK$ be the pullback comparison followed by the point-sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Then
$$J_{y,M}(d_K)b_{G_E^mK}(t_{y,m,K}\otimes_E M)=t_{y,m,TK}b_K.$$
These are comparisons in the framework rationalized categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with the same identity and tower identifications as the specified scalar comparisons.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-return-frobenius-cancellation] to the specified $y$ to obtain $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$ and $g_X^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$, including the geometric/arithmetic inverse convention. Use $I^{(0)}=1$, $I^{(j+1)}_N=\iota_{U_\Lambda^jN}I^{(j)}_N$ and the return comparison $v_{\Lambda,K}$ of [lem-trf-iterated-return-transport-scalar-calculus]. The definition of the requested map is $t_{y,m,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(v_{\Lambda,K})I^{(m)}_{P_\Lambda K}$; that lemma gives its naturality at finite, integral and raw rational stages.

proof.text: The finite chain-map identity of [lem-trf-finite-return-frobenius-cancellation] is exactly $t_{y,m,K}=J_{y,\Lambda}(\kappa^{(m)}_K)\rho_{y,m,K}$, with the specified absolute-Frobenius cancellation and no scalar rescaling. For an integral $K$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] each $Q_n$ is a flat-term K-flat complex of $(A_{E,n})_X$-modules; since $Q$ is K-flat it represents the derived reduction $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, which lies in $D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$ by the definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Hence the finite identity of [lem-trf-finite-return-frobenius-cancellation] applies to every $Q_n$ as an equality of chain maps. Apply [lem-trf-local-normalization-strict-realization] to this simultaneous quotient system: its hypotheses are the two scheme equalities from Step 1 and these chain-map identities. It gives equality of the actual strict maps, compatibility with quotient transitions and derived coefficient comparisons, and identifies their integral realizations with the specified successive transport and normalized map. Its rationalization clause proves the equality at $E$. The reductions are only bounded constructible; no finite Tor-amplitude or perfectness condition is imposed.

proof.text:
For $E\subset M$ use $a,d,\delta,\beta,v,I$ with the exact meanings in [lem-trf-iterated-return-transport-scalar-calculus]. By [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], $b_K=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(a_K)\beta_{P_EK}$ and $\beta$ is natural. Expanding $t$ and moving $\beta$ across $v_E$ rewrites $J_{y,M}(d_K)b_{G_E^mK}(t_{y,m,K}\otimes M)$ as
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}\!\left(P_M(d_K)a_{G_E^mK}T_s(v_{E,K})\right)\beta_{U_E^mP_EK}(I_{P_EK}^{(m)}\otimes M).$$
Substitute the return-square equation and iterated point equation of that lemma. This becomes $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(v_{M,TK}U_M^m(a_K))I_{T_sP_EK}^{(m)}\beta_{P_EK}$. Naturality of $I^{(m)}$ for $a_K$ makes it $t_{y,m,TK}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(a_K)\beta_{P_EK}=t_{y,m,TK}b_K$. The cited equations respect the specified identity and coefficient-tower associators, so this substitution proves those compatibilities too.

lean.note: Successor indices cover every positive m and finite coefficient exponent. Normalization unfolds the finite, integral, rational, whole strict-system and scalar equations. Helper definitions give the prescribed canonical maps; chosen data are uniquely characterized, never arbitrary maps. Finite transport is recursively composed from frobeniusPointTransportFinite, the unit-normalized pointPowerPullbackModel and proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition; finiteOrdinary and StrictFormula use this same successive iterate.
